$comment: During the Events phase each player, in turn order, reveals one card and resolves it (see deck below). The card's scope decides who it hits: a global card the third player draws still hits everyone. Each card carries plain text for the tabletop game and a machine-readable effects array so the digital version can resolve it automatically.

scopes.name: Global
scopes.summary: Applies to every player, whoever drew it.

scopes.name: Local
scopes.summary: Applies to one region of the board - roll for the region.

scopes.name: Targeted
scopes.summary: Applies to the player who drew it - except crime cards, which target the leader.

scopes.name: Offer
scopes.summary: An opportunity. The drawer decides first; if they pass, it goes round in turn order.

effectTypes.$comment: The vocabulary the digital engine understands. Keep new cards inside it where you can.
effectTypes.effort: Change effort dice or hours for matching workers.
effectTypes.price: Shift a commodity family's price band.
effectTypes.building: Damage, destroy or halt a building.
effectTypes.tool: Add wear to or break tools.
effectTypes.health: Damage or heal characters and travelling figures.
effectTypes.discovery: Widen or shrink a result band on the discovery tables - see data/discovery.json.

cards.name: Hard Frost
cards.text: A cold snap grips the map. Crops stall and outdoor work is miserable.
mitigations: Workers living in a brick house or manor are unaffected.
A town with 2+ fuel in stock ignores the effort penalty.

cards.name: Drought
cards.text: The wells run low. Nothing green does well this year.
mitigations: A town with a well loses no water.
Towns on a coast or marsh tile - anywhere with fresh water - are unaffected.

cards.name: Long Summer
cards.text: A gift of a season.

cards.name: Storms at Sea
cards.text: Nothing sails this round, and something already at sea does not arrive.
mitigations: Cargo in a harbour tile is safe.

cards.name: Flood
cards.text: The river takes back its floodplain.

cards.name: Earthquake
cards.text: The hills shrug.

effects.text: Halve the build track - the building stops until it is repaired.

cards.name: Wildfire
cards.text: Fire runs through the timber.
mitigations: A town with a well or on a water-access tile rolls at 5+ instead.

cards.name: Mine Collapse
cards.text: A gallery comes down.
mitigations: A dwarf player halts for 1 round and loses no worker.

cards.name: Warehouse Heist
cards.text: Thieves empty a warehouse in the night.

effects.text: Lose half the contents of one warehouse, owner's choice of which items.

mitigations: A watchtower in that town cancels this card once per game.
Soldiers garrisoned in the town halve the loss.

cards.name: Caravan Robbery
cards.text: Bandits on the road.

effects.text: The highest-value cargo token in transit by road is taken.

mitigations: An escorting soldier rolls a combat die; on 4+ the robbery fails.

cards.name: Train Heist
cards.text: They knew the timetable.

cards.name: Piracy
cards.text: A sail on the horizon, and it is not a friendly one.

cards.name: Smuggling Ring
cards.text: Someone offers to move goods without the market's cut - and without any guarantees.

effects.text: Sell up to 6 bulk at 150% of base value.

cards.name: Wolf Pack
cards.text: Something is taking the livestock.
mitigations: Any soldier or hero in the region may fight the pack instead of losing animals.

cards.name: Boar in the Fields
cards.text: It has been in the crops for a week.

cards.name: Dragon Sighting
cards.text: A shape passes over the mountains. Everyone finds somewhere else to be.

cards.name: Raiders
cards.text: An armed band comes over the border at whoever looks richest.
mitigations: Palisade grants +1 defence die. Garrisoned soldiers defend automatically.

cards.name: Border Dispute
cards.text: Two towns claim the same ground.

effects.text: Both players roll 2 combat dice. The loser gives the winner one tile's worth of infrastructure.

cards.name: Mercenaries for Hire
cards.text: Swords, cheap, for as long as the coin lasts.

cards.name: Plague
cards.text: It moves faster than anyone can plan for.
mitigations: A town holding a Healing Draught spends it to ignore this card entirely.

cards.name: Migrants
cards.text: A column of families on the road, looking for somewhere with food.

effects.condition: you must have housing and 4 food in that town

cards.name: Strike
cards.text: They want feeding properly.
mitigations: Serve ale or wine at an inn to end the strike immediately.

cards.name: Festival
cards.text: A week of noise and spending.

effects.condition: if the town serves any drink

cards.name: Travelling Master
cards.text: A master will take an apprentice, for a price.

effects.text: Train one specialist without a guildhall.

cards.name: Iron Shortage
cards.text: Everyone wants metal and nobody has any.

cards.name: Glut
cards.text: A bumper year somewhere else. Prices fall through the floor.

cards.name: Foreign Demand
cards.text: A distant city sends buyers. Roll to see what they want.

cards.name: Tax Levy
cards.text: The crown remembers you exist.

effects.text: Pay 3 coin per completed building. If you cannot pay, gain 1 unrest per unpaid building.

cards.name: Ley Surge
cards.text: The ground hums for a week.

cards.name: Curdled Brew
cards.text: Something went wrong in the alembic.

cards.name: Wandering Wizard
cards.text: He will trade knowledge for something shiny.

effects.text: Take any 2 potions from items.json for free.

cards.name: Camp Fever
cards.text: Something in the water at last night's camp. Your travelling party wakes shivering.

effects.text: Every figure and character in one of your travelling parties takes 2 damage.

mitigations: A healer character in the party shrugs it off: no damage, full speed.
Spend a Healing Draught or Physic Tonic to cancel the card.

cards.name: Marsh Ague
cards.text: The ague drifts out of the fens with the evening mist, and the village bell rings thin all week.

effects.condition: only towns on or adjacent to a marsh tile

mitigations: A town with an infirmary and a fed healer loses no worker.
A Physic Tonic cancels the card for one town.

cards.name: The Grey Pox
cards.text: It starts in one market square and is everywhere by week's end. Whole streets shutter; the carts stop coming.

effects.condition: every town with 4 or more workers loses one

mitigations: A town with an infirmary and a fed healer loses no worker.
A Healing Draught spent by a town cancels its loss.
This is the card that makes the infirmary worth its parchment.

cards.name: Impure Smelt
cards.text: A bad seam of flux stone in every furnace this week. The metal pours grey and snaps like slate.

effects.text: Every tool used this round takes double wear.
Any tool forged this round is marked brittle: it breaks when its durability track reaches half, not zero.

mitigations: A smelter or blacksmith burning coal this round is unaffected - coal runs hot enough to burn the impurities out. Peat and charcoal do not.
A smith specialist may spend 2 hours re-tempering to clear one brittle mark.

cards.name: Blood Moon
cards.text: The moon rises rust-red and the wild things move under it.

effects.text: Monster bands on every discovery table widen by 3 for two rounds.

mitigations: A party carrying a lit lantern is never surprised: it may always choose to withdraw before a monster encounter begins.

cards.name: The Quiet Season
cards.text: The wild goes still. Hunters come home early, and nothing follows them home.

effects.text: Monster bands on every discovery table shrink by 2 for two rounds.

deck.$totalNote: Sum of every card's copies. The previous figure of 58 had drifted from the data - which is exactly why the annex is generated now.
deck.when: In the Events phase, each player in turn order reveals one card and resolves it before the Labour Roll.

lateGame.extra: From round 13, the first player each round reveals and resolves a second card.

deck.reshuffle: When the deck runs out, shuffle the discard pile and carry on.
designNotes: Every player turning a card means every player owns a piece of the round's weather. A global card is global whoever drew it; a targeted card is the drawer's problem.
Weather and market cards are the common ones - they should feel like the seasons turning, not like being punished.
Crime cards target the leader by default. That is the catch-up mechanism, and it is deliberate.
Every disaster card should have at least one mitigation a player could have bought in advance. Being wiped out should always be traceable to a decision.
Discovery-band cards (Blood Moon, The Quiet Season) are the dial on how dangerous the wild feels. Add copies to taste.
